newsitem.title: INDIA: India's EIH, HK firm in resorts tie-up.
newsitem.headline: India's EIH, HK firm in resorts tie-up.

text.p: India's East India Hotels (EIH) said on Friday that it had formed a joint venture with Hong Kong's CCA International Ltd to develop, market and manage private clubs and resorts in India.

"We have entered into a strategic alliance with CCA and have set up a joint venture company, CCA Leisure Services Pvt Ltd," EIH vice chairman and managing director P.R.S. Oberoi told a news conference.

He said the initial capital of the joint venture will be 10 million rupees ($280,000), with CCA holding 60 percent and EIH, one of India's leading hotel chains that uses the Oberoi brand name, and its affiliated companies holding the rest.
The venture will be a management company to start with, and will consider taking equity in privately-owned clubs at a later date, he added.

Oberoi said that the venture would initially manage EIH's business lounges in several of its properties called Belvedere Clubs and a golf club and resort, partly owned by EIH, near Bangalore in South India.
"The joint venture will have between three and five clubs under its management in two years," CCA's managing director Helmut Knipp said.
He said that CCA operates 28 private clubs and resorts, including two in Europe. It owns several of the resorts and clubs it operates.
